newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 17.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Police commander general denies that a police agent was sent into parliament to carry out an investigation, as denounced by some politicians. "We are provoked by a criminal world we are not able to defeat, a world made of meddlers ... businessmen and mafia bosses" (all).
* Banker Francesco Pacini Battaglia, who was recently arrested on corruption charges along with state railway managing director Lorenzo Necci, was an informer for Milan magistates (all).

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi says Pds secretary general Massimo D'Alema should go ahead with a proposal for a bicameral all-party commission to carry out constitutional reforms. But Berlusconi allies are split over striking a possible deal with centre left parties (all).
* In the 1997 budget, there will be no new taxes on the first house owned by families (all).
* Industrial output fell by one percent in the first 8 months of 1996 (all).
* The Treasury is optimistic over the sale of Banco di Napoli, after Standar & Poor's said it might upgrade the bank (Sole 24 Ore).

* Chairman of antitrust authority Giuliano Amato says the privatisation of telecoms holding Stet is a "political game". "If someone doesn't want the privatisation of Stet, and knows that before the privatisation the antitrust authority has to be set up, they can try to delay the launch of the authority". (La Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
